## Overview

Two groups of family-based immigrant visa categories, immediate relatives and family preference, are provided under the provisions of U.S. immigration law, specifically the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).  You may wish to review our [Directory of Visa Categories](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html) steps on [usvisas.state.gov](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html) to learn more about these two categories of immigrant visas, as well as other types of immigrant visas to the United States.

To apply for an immediate relative or family preference immigrant visa, follow the steps on the [Immigrant Visa Process](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/immigrate/the-immigrant-visa-process.html) on usvisas.state.gov.  Once you have completed those steps, review the instructions given to you by the National Visa Center (NVC), along with the information presented on this website, for further guidance and instructions.

## The Interview

After you have completed the steps on the [Immigrant Visa Process](http://travel.state.gov/content/visas/en/immigrate/immigrant-process/petition.html) on usvisas.state.gov, including paying the necessary fees and submitting the required immigrant visa application form (DS-260), Affidavit of Support, and supporting documents to the National Visa Center (NVC), they will review your file for completeness. Once your case becomes qualified for an interview, NVC will work with us to schedule an interview appointment for you.

You can learn more about the [interview process](http://travel.state.gov/content/visas/en/immigrate/immigrant-process/interview.html) on usvisas.state.gov.

 

**BRING YOUR DOCUMENTS** 

Every applicant must bring certain documents to the interview.  These include: 

- Two visa photos taken within the last 6 months on white background. ([Find photo instructions here](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/photos.html)*)* 
- All original, government-registered civil documents, including: 
  - Birth Certificate 
  - Petitioner’s birth certificate (for IR5 and F4 cases)
  - Marriage Certificate 
  - Divorce Certificates 
  - Death Certificates of Spouses 
  - Valid Police Certificate  

&nbsp;

- Evidence of your relationship with the Petitioner, which can include, but is not limited to: 
  - Photographs 
  - Call or chat logs 
  - Remittance receipts 

**FAILURE TO BRING YOUR REQUIRED DOCUMENTS MAY RESULT IN DELAYS AND YOUR VISA BEING DENIED UNDER SECTION 221(G) OF THE IMMIGRATION AND NATIONALITY ACT UNTIL YOU PROVIDE THE APPROPRIATE DOCUMENTATION.**

- 

## Case Status

At the end of your immigrant visa interview, the consular officer will inform you whether your visa application is approved or denied.

Some visa applications require further [administrative processing](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/administrative-processing-information.html), which takes additional time after the visa applicant’s interview by a consular officer. Applicants are advised of this requirement during their interview. When administrative processing is required, the timing will vary based on the individual circumstances of each case.  You can [check the status](https://ceac.state.gov/CEACStatTracker/Status.aspx?eQs=o/iS8zDpeAKjMWCuebHqOw==) of your visa application on [ceac.state.gov](https://ceac.state.gov/ceac/).

If your visa has been denied, you may find useful information on [Ineligibilities and Waivers](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/visa-information-resources/waivers.html) on usvisas.state.gov.

If you choose to respond to a Request for Evidence (RFE) letter from United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) by having DNA testing done, the collection in Bangladesh will be handled by the USCIS office in Dhaka and not the Consular Section.  If you received an RFE letter from USCIS but have not yet scheduled a DNA collection appointment, you should follow the instructions in the letter or review the [USCIS Dhaka Field Office website](https://www.uscis.gov/about-us/find-a-uscis-office/international-offices/bangladesh-uscis-dhaka-field-office) for details on how to make arrangements for DNA collection.

DNA testing requests related to an immigrant visa application will continue to be overseen by the consular section where that application has been filed.  Applicants for whom DNA testing has been recommended will receive a detailed letter with more information about the process.  Please follow the instructions on that letter to facilitate a timely process.

## After the Interview

If your visa has been approved, you will be informed how and when your passport and visa will be returned to you.  Carefully review [After the Interview](http://travel.state.gov/content/visas/en/immigrate/immigrant-process/interview/after.html) on usvisas.state.gov to learn what to do when you receive your visa, entering the United States, paying the USCIS immigrant fee for your Legal Permanent Resident (LPR) Card (aka “Green Card”).
